diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in etcd, discovered by Strix's autonomous AI agent. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-33413, allows unauthorized access to sensitive cluster operations, posing a high risk to systems with network access to the gRPC endpoint. The flaw is due to missing authorization checks in the etcd server architecture's applier chain, specifically affecting the Alarm, Compaction, and LeaseGrant methods. Organizations using etcd are advised to apply the March 2026 security patch to mitigate the risk.
doc_summary: An autonomous AI security agent developed by Strix discovered a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in etcd, tracked as CVE-2026-33413, with a CVSS score of 8.8. This flaw allows unauthenticated or under-privileged users to invoke sensitive cluster operations, exposing systems to severe disruption if an attacker has network access to the client gRPC endpoint on port 2379. The vulnerability specifically affects the Alarm, Compaction, and LeaseGrant methods due to a flaw in the etcd server architecture's applier chain. Strix identified the issue on March 3, 2026, and the etcd security team released a patch in March 2026. Organizations using etcd are urged to update to the latest patched versions immediately.

The extensions masquerade as legitimate tools like Telegram clients and YouTube enhancers. Five extensions use Chrome's declarativeNetRequest API to strip security headers. Title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Axios Library (CVE-2026-40175)

Victim.Description: Applications using vulnerable versions of the Axios library, potentially across various industries.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to outdated Axios versions.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Axios library, allowing adversaries to execute remote code and compromise cloud infrastructure. The adversary exploits a lack of HTTP header sanitization, combined with SSRF and request smuggling techniques, to exfiltrate AWS metadata and achieve full cloud account compromise. The attack targets applications using vulnerable Axios versions, affecting a wide range of deployments.
doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-40175, has been discovered in the Axios HTTP client library, exposing applications to Remote Code Execution (RCE) and full cloud infrastructure compromise. This flaw, with a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.9, allows attackers to bypass AWS IMDSv2 security controls to exfiltrate sensitive cloud metadata. The vulnerability is rooted in an unrestricted cloud metadata exfiltration flaw via a header injection chain within the axios npm package. The core issue resides in the library’s header processing components, specifically within the lib/adapters/http.js file, involving a lack of HTTP header sanitization (CWE-113), combined with Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) capabilities (CWE-918) and request smuggling (CWE-444). The exploit relies on a “Gadget” chain, where polluted Object.prototype properties from third-party dependencies like body-parser, qs, or minimist are merged into Axios configuration, transforming into an HTTP request smuggling payload. The PoC demonstrates exploitation targeting cloud environments, enabling attackers to smuggle a secondary PUT request to the AWS EC2 Metadata Service, bypassing AWS IMDSv2 protections, retrieving session tokens, and achieving full cloud account compromise. All Axios versions prior to 1.13.2 are vulnerable. Mitigation involves updating to version 1.15.0 or later, which enforces strict header validation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of a vulnerability in the Axios library, allowing adversaries to execute remote code and exfiltrate cloud metadata. The adversary uses a 'Gadget' chain to inject malicious headers into HTTP requests, bypassing AWS IMDSv2 protections and retrieving session tokens. The attack culminates in full cloud account compromise, with potential secondary impacts such as authentication bypass and cache poisoning.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and tools as key indicators. The IP address 169.254.169.254 is targeted for AWS metadata exfiltration, while the Axios library is exploited for remote code execution. These indicators are crucial for detecting and mitigating the attack, as they represent the adversary's methods and infrastructure.

doc_summary: Adobe has released an emergency security update for Acrobat Reader to fix a vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-34621, that has been exploited in zero-day attacks since at least December. The flaw allows malicious PDF files to bypass sandbox restrictions and invoke privileged JavaScript APIs, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution. The exploit enables reading and stealing arbitrary files. No user interaction is required beyond opening the malicious PDF. Specifically, the exploit abuses APIs like util.readFileIntoStream() to read arbitrary local files and RSS.addFeed() to exfiltrate data and fetch additional attacker-controlled code. The security issue was discovered by Haifei Li, founder of the EXPMON exploit detection system, after someone submitted a sample for analysis. The sample was sent to VirusTotal three days before, where only five out of 64 security vendors detected it at the time. Security researcher Gi7w0rm observed the exploit in the wild leveraging Russian-language documents with oil and gas industry lures. Following the receipt of Li’s report, Adobe published a security bulletin over the weekend, assigning the vulnerability the CVE-2026-34621 tracker. Although the flaw was initially rated critical (9.6) with a network attack vector, Adobe subsequently lowered the severity to 8.6 after changing the vector to local. The vendor listed the following Windows and macOS products as impacted. Adobe recommends that users of the above software update their applications through ‘Help > Check for Updates,’ which triggers an automated update. Alternatively, users may download an Acrobat Reader installer from Adobe’s website. No workarounds or mitigations were listed in the bulletin, so applying the security updates is the only recommended action. However, users should always be wary of PDF files sent from unsolicited sources and open them in sandboxed environments when suspicious.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with the weaponization of a PDF file exploiting CVE-2026-34621. Delivery occurs through the distribution of malicious PDFs, leading to exploitation by bypassing sandbox restrictions. doc_summary: Unknown threat actors compromised the CPUID website, which hosts popular hardware monitoring tools like CPU-Z and HWMonitor, to distribute malicious executables and deploy the STX RAT. The incident lasted from April 9 to April 10, 2023, with download URLs replaced by links to malicious websites. The attack leveraged a compromised side API, leading to the distribution of trojanized software containing a legitimate signed executable and a malicious DLL named 'CRYPTBASE.dll'. The DLL contacts an external server, performs anti-sandbox checks, and executes additional payloads to deploy STX RAT, which has HVNC and infostealer capabilities. The C2 server address was reused from a prior campaign involving trojanized FileZilla installers. Kaspersky identified over 150 victims, including individuals and organizations in retail, manufacturing, consulting, telecommunications, and agriculture, primarily in Brazil, Russia, and China. The attackers' reuse of the infection chain and domain names facilitated detection.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves Google's implementation of Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in Chrome 146 to protect against info-stealing malware. The adversary is characterized by the use of infostealer malware, such as LummaC2, targeting session cookies. The capability involves malware that harvests session cookies, while the infrastructure and victim details are not significantly detailed. The victim is primarily users of Google Chrome on Windows and macOS, with the industry being technology and the geography being global.
doc_summary: Google has introduced Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) in Chrome 146 for Windows to prevent info-stealing malware from accessing session cookies. This feature will be available for macOS in a future release. DBSC links a user's session to their hardware using security chips like TPM on Windows and Secure Enclave on macOS. The unique keys generated by these chips cannot be exported, rendering stolen session data useless without the private key. Google reports a decline in session theft during a year of testing DBSC with partners like Okta. The protocol, developed with Microsoft, is designed to be private and prevents user activity correlation across sessions. Websites can adopt this security by updating their backend endpoints. Specifications are available on the W3C website, and an explainer is on GitHub.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain stages for this incident are not explicitly detailed in the text. However, the adversary's objective is to harvest session cookies using infostealer malware. The introduction of DBSC in Chrome 146 aims to disrupt this by binding session credentials to hardware, making stolen session data useless without the private key. This enhancement targets the exploitation and actions on objectives stages by preventing unauthorized access to user accounts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is not explicitly detailed in the text. However, the introduction of DBSC in Chrome 146 aims to increase the difficulty for adversaries by binding session credentials to hardware, making it challenging to exploit stolen session cookies. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains limits the ability to provide a detailed Pyramid of Pain analysis.

Title: Figure Data Breach Exposes 967,200 Email Records

Victim.Description: Figure, a financial services company, exposed email records.

diamond_model_summary: The Figure data breach involved adversaries leveraging exposed email records for credential stuffing, phishing, and social engineering attacks. The adversaries used publicly available tools like Evilginx, Modlishka, and Muraena to bypass traditional MFA systems. The breach highlights the need for authentication systems that verify human presence, such as Token's Biometric Assured Identity platform.
doc_summary: In February 2026, a data breach at Figure, a financial services company, exposed 967,200 email records. The breach did not involve any exploits or zero-day vulnerabilities. Adversaries can leverage these records for credential stuffing, phishing, and social engineering attacks. The breach highlights the limitations of traditional MFA systems, which can be bypassed using real-time phishing relay attacks. Tools like Evilginx, Modlishka, and Muraena facilitate these attacks. The incident underscores the need for authentication systems that verify human presence, such as Token's Biometric Assured Identity platform, which combines biometrics, hardware-bound cryptographic authentication, and physical proximity verification.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain began with the exposure of email records, which adversaries used for credential stuffing and phishing. The adversaries exploited human factors through social engineering, bypassing traditional MFA systems using real-time phishing relay attacks. The attack chain underscores the limitations of legacy MFA and the need for advanced authentication mechanisms.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain analysis reveals that adversaries used tools like Evilginx, Modlishka, and Muraena to execute their attacks. These tools facilitate credential stuffing and phishing, making them significant indicators of compromise. The breach highlights the need for advanced authentication systems that verify human presence to mitigate such attacks.

Title: Malicious Update in Smart Slider 3 Pro Plugin for WordPress and Joomla

Victim.Description: Websites using Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin for WordPress and Joomla were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary who compromised the update system of the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin, distributing a malicious version with backdoors. The adversary's capability included a multi-layered malware toolkit embedded in the plugin, allowing for remote command execution and credential theft. The infrastructure used was the compromised update system, and the victims were websites using the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin for WordPress and Joomla.
doc_summary: Hackers compromised the update system for the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin, affecting version 3.5.1.35. The malicious update included multiple backdoors, created a hidden admin user, and stole sensitive data. The attack was distributed on April 7, 2023. PatchStack analysis revealed a multi-layered toolkit embedded in the plugin's main file, allowing remote command execution and credential theft. Persistence was achieved through hidden admin accounts, must-use plugins, and backdoors in theme files. The vendor recommends updating to version 3.5.1.36 or reverting to earlier versions. Administrators should assume full site compromise, remove unauthorized users, and reset passwords. The incident highlights the importance of securing update systems and implementing strong security measures.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the adversary compromising the update system of the Smart Slider 3 Pro plugin, weaponizing the update to include a malicious toolkit. The delivery stage involved distributing the malicious update to users. Exploitation occurred as the update installed backdoors and created hidden admin accounts. Installation involved embedding the malware toolkit within the plugin. Command and control were established through the backdoors, allowing the adversary to execute commands and steal credentials. The final stage, actions on objectives, involved the theft of sensitive site information.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators such as the malicious plugin update, hidden admin accounts, and backdoors in theme files. These indicators represent different levels of difficulty for the adversary to change. The malicious update and hidden admin accounts are relatively easy for the adversary to modify, while the backdoors in theme files and must-use plugins provide more persistent challenges. The incident highlights the importance of detecting and responding to these indicators to disrupt the adversary's operations.

Title: VENOM PhaaS Platform Targets C-Suite Executives

Victim.Description: C-suite executives targeted across multiple industries.

diamond_model_summary: The VENOM PhaaS platform is used by threat actors to target C-suite executives across multiple industries. The operation is sophisticated, employing phishing emails that impersonate Microsoft SharePoint notifications and use QR codes to bypass traditional scanning tools. The adversary's capability includes advanced phishing techniques such as adversary-in-the-middle attacks and device-code phishing, allowing them to harvest credentials and maintain persistent access. The infrastructure is closed-access, reducing exposure to researchers, and the victims are high-value targets, specifically CEOs, CFOs, and VPs.
doc_summary: Threat actors using a previously undocumented phishing-as-a-service platform called VENOM are targeting credentials of C-suite executives across multiple industries. The operation has been active since at least last November and targets specific individuals such as CEOs, CFOs, or VPs. VENOM is closed access, not promoted on public channels, reducing exposure to researchers. Phishing emails impersonate Microsoft SharePoint notifications, including random HTML noise and fake email threads. A QR code rendered in Unicode is used to bypass scanning tools, shifting the attack to mobile devices. The target's email is double Base64-encoded in the URL fragment, making it invisible to server-side logs. Scanning the QR code leads to a landing page filtering out non-targets. Real targets are redirected to a credential-harvesting page proxying a Microsoft login flow, capturing credentials and MFA codes. VENOM also uses a device-code phishing tactic, tricking victims into approving access for a rogue device. This method is effective and resistant to password resets. VENOM establishes persistent access by registering a new device or obtaining a token. MFA is insufficient; FIDO2 authentication and stricter conditional access policies are recommended.
kill_chain_summary: The VENOM PhaaS operation follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify high-value C-suite targets. Weaponization involves crafting phishing emails and QR codes. Delivery is executed through spearphishing emails impersonating Microsoft SharePoint notifications. Exploitation occurs when victims scan the QR code, leading to credential harvesting. Installation is achieved by registering new devices or obtaining tokens for persistent access. Command and control are maintained through a proxy that relays credentials and MFA codes. Actions on objectives focus on harvesting credentials and maintaining access to executive accounts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The VENOM PhaaS operation presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. The use of QR codes and adversary-in-the-middle techniques complicates detection and response. The operation's closed-access infrastructure and sophisticated phishing tactics make it difficult to identify specific indicators such as IP addresses or domain names. The reliance on advanced phishing techniques and the targeting of high-value individuals increase the difficulty of disrupting the operation. The lack of specific indicators in the provided text limits the ability to populate the Pyramid of Pain with concrete data.

Title: Analysis of CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

Victim.Description: Organizations across various sectors are affected by the rapid exploitation of vulnerabilities.

diamond_model_summary: The analysis reveals a significant operational failure in the current cybersecurity model, where adversaries exploit vulnerabilities faster than they can be patched. The adversaries leverage AI to enhance their capabilities, creating a high level of sophistication. The victims are organizations across various sectors globally, facing high impact severity due to rapid exploitation. The capability of adversaries includes exploiting vulnerabilities like Spring4Shell and Cisco IOS XE, often before patches are available.
doc_summary: The analysis of CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities over the past four years highlights critical vulnerabilities remaining open at Day 7, increasing from 56% to 63%. Despite increased ticket closures, the operational model is flawed. Of 52 tracked weaponized vulnerabilities, 88% were patched slower than exploited. The average Time-to-Exploit is negative seven days, indicating adversaries weaponize vulnerabilities before patches exist. The report identifies a 'Manual Tax' where long-tail assets extend exposure. Risk Mass and Average Window of Exposure are proposed as new metrics. AI-powered attackers pose a significant threat, necessitating autonomous, closed-loop risk operations. The traditional scan-and-report model is outdated, requiring an end-to-end Risk Operations Center.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain analysis identifies significant activity in the reconnaissance, weaponization, and exploitation stages. Adversaries rapidly identify and weaponize vulnerabilities, exploiting them before patches are available. The tactics and techniques employed include active scanning and vulnerability exploitation. Title: Compromise of CPUID API Leading to Malicious Distribution of CPU-Z and HWMonitor

Victim.Description: Users of CPU-Z and HWMonitor, potentially millions, were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved a sophisticated adversary targeting CPUID's API to distribute trojanized versions of popular software tools. The adversary demonstrated advanced capabilities in malware distribution and evasion, leveraging compromised domains and external storage services. Victims included users of CPU-Z and HWMonitor, with potential data theft as a strategic objective.
doc_summary: Hackers compromised the CPUID API, altering download links on the official website to distribute malicious executables for CPU-Z and HWMonitor. The attack involved a trojanized version of HWiNFO, using a Russian installer with an Inno Setup wrapper. The malware is multi-staged, operates in-memory, and evades EDRs by proxying NTDLL functionality from a .NET assembly. The same threat group previously targeted FileZilla users. The malicious ZIP file is flagged by antivirus engines as Tedy Trojan or Artemis Trojan. CPUID has since fixed the issue, restoring clean versions of the affected tools.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify widely used software, followed by weaponization of a trojanized HWiNFO installer. Delivery was achieved through altered download links, leading to installation on victim systems. The malware operated in-memory, using advanced evasion techniques, and potentially acted as an infostealer.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like cpuid-dot-com and malware families such as Tedy Trojan and Artemis Trojan. The adversary's use of advanced evasion techniques and in-memory operations increases the difficulty of detection and response, highlighting the need for robust monitoring and threat intelligence capabilities.

Title: LucidRook Malware Campaign Targeting Taiwan NGOs and Universities
Tools: Trend Micro Worry-Free Business Security Services

Victim.Description: Non-governmental organizations and universities in Taiwan are targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The LucidRook campaign is attributed to the threat group UAT-10362, targeting NGOs and universities in Taiwan. The adversary employs sophisticated techniques, including spear-phishing and modular malware design, to achieve espionage objectives. The infrastructure involves phishing emails and FTP for data exfiltration, while victims are primarily in the education and NGO sectors.
doc_summary: A new Lua-based malware named LucidRook is being used in spear-phishing campaigns targeting non-governmental organizations and universities in Taiwan. Cisco Talos researchers attribute the malware to a threat group tracked as UAT-10362, describing them as a capable adversary with mature operational tradecraft. The attacks were observed in October 2025, utilizing phishing emails with password-protected archives. Two infection chains were identified: one using an LNK shortcut file delivering LucidPawn, and another using a fake antivirus executable impersonating Trend Micro Worry-Free Business Security Services. The LNK-based attack employs decoy documents mimicking Taiwanese government letters. LucidPawn decrypts and deploys a legitimate executable renamed to mimic Microsoft Edge, along with a malicious DLL for sideloading LucidRook. LucidRook's modular design and built-in Lua execution environment allow it to retrieve and execute second-stage payloads as Lua bytecode, enhancing stealth and operational security. The binary is heavily obfuscated, complicating reverse-engineering efforts. LucidRook performs system reconnaissance, collecting and encrypting data for exfiltration via FTP. A related tool, LucidKnight, abuses Gmail GMTP for data exfiltration. Cisco Talos concludes with medium confidence that these attacks are part of a targeted intrusion campaign.
kill_chain_summary: The LucidRook campaign follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through system data collection. Weaponization involves the use of modular malware with Lua execution. Delivery is achieved via spear-phishing emails, leading to exploitation through malicious file execution. Installation occurs via DLL sideloading, followed by command and control using FTP and Gmail GMTP. Finally, actions on objectives involve data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The LucidRook campaign presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain, with obfuscated files and modular malware design complicating detection. The use of FTP and Gmail GMTP for command and control adds complexity to network monitoring. The campaign's reliance on spear-phishing and DLL sideloading highlights the need for robust detection and remediation strategies.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new evolution in the GlassWorm campaign, utilizing a Zig dropper to infect integrated development environments (IDEs) on developers' machines. Title: Google's Device Bound Session Credentials to Combat Session Theft

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves cybercriminals targeting session cookies for unauthorized access. Google's Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) aims to mitigate this by binding session cookies to specific devices using hardware-backed security modules. This approach reduces the effectiveness of malware like Atomic, Lumma, and Vidar Stealer, which are used to exfiltrate session cookies.
doc_summary: Google has introduced Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) to enhance security in its Chrome browser, initially available for Windows users. This feature aims to prevent session theft by cryptographically binding session cookies to specific devices using hardware-backed security modules like Trusted Platform Module (TPM) and Secure Enclave. Session theft typically involves malware such as Atomic, Lumma, and Vidar Stealer, which exfiltrate session cookies for unauthorized access. DBSC ensures that stolen cookies become useless by requiring proof of possession of a private key. Google plans to expand DBSC to macOS and other devices, emphasizing privacy and minimal data exchange to prevent cross-site tracking.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain stages relevant to this incident include the potential for malware delivery and installation on victim systems to exfiltrate session cookies. Google's DBSC aims to disrupt this chain by ensuring that stolen cookies become useless without the corresponding private key. This reduces the impact of session theft and unauthorized access to online accounts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools like Atomic, Lumma, and Vidar Stealer, which are used to exfiltrate session cookies. doc_summary: Threat actors have been exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in Adobe Reader using malicious PDF documents since December 2025. The exploit, detailed by EXPMON's Haifei Li, involves a sophisticated PDF named 'Invoice540.pdf' first seen on VirusTotal on November 28, 2025. A second sample appeared on March 23, 2026. The attack uses social engineering, with Russian language lures related to the oil and gas industry, to trick users into opening the PDF. Once opened, it executes obfuscated JavaScript to harvest data and receive payloads. The exploit allows remote code execution and sandbox escape, confirmed to work on the latest Adobe Reader version. Data is exfiltrated to a remote server at '169.40.2[.]68:45191'. The attack's full potential remains unknown as no response was received from the server, possibly due to environmental criteria not being met.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with weaponization of a zero-day exploit in Adobe Reader, delivered via malicious PDFs. Exploitation occurs through social engineering, leading to execution of obfuscated JavaScript. Installation of additional payloads is facilitated, followed by command and control communication with a remote server. The attack's objectives include data exfiltration and potential further exploitation, with a focus on the Oil & Gas industry.

doc_summary: Google has released an urgent security update for its Chrome browser, addressing multiple critical vulnerabilities. The update, version 147, was promoted to the stable channel for Windows, Mac, and Linux users on April 7, 2026. The most severe threats are two critical vulnerabilities in the WebML component, tracked as CVE-2026-5858 and CVE-2026-5859, involving heap buffer and integer overflows. These vulnerabilities could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code and take full control of affected systems. Google awarded $43,000 bug bounties to the researchers who discovered these flaws. Additional high-severity bugs were found in the V8 JavaScript engine, WebRTC, Media, Blink, and Skia components. Google paid tens of thousands of dollars in rewards to ethical hackers to prevent these issues from being exploited. The update is rolling out globally, and users are advised to update their browsers immediately. Google will keep technical details restricted to allow time for patch installation and protect other software projects using the same libraries.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in Chrome's WebML component through specially crafted web pages. Google has issued a critical update to address these issues, emphasizing the importance of immediate patching to protect users.

doc_summary: GitLab has released a critical security update addressing multiple vulnerabilities in its Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) platforms. The update is crucial for self-managed GitLab instances to prevent potential exploitation. The most critical flaw, CVE-2026-5173, involves an exposed method vulnerability in websocket connections, allowing authenticated attackers to invoke unintended server-side methods. The patches for versions 18.10.3, 18.9.5, and 18.8.9 address twelve security flaws, including high-severity denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerabilities in the Terraform state lock API and GraphQL API. Medium-severity issues affecting data integrity and user privacy, such as a code injection flaw in Code Quality reports and cross-site scripting (XSS) in analytics dashboards, are also resolved. Administrators are urged to upgrade to the latest patch release to maintain security hygiene and protect against both authenticated insiders and unauthenticated external threats.

doc_summary: SonicWall has issued a critical security advisory for its SMA1000 series appliances, addressing four vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-4112, CVE-2026-4113, CVE-2026-4114, and CVE-2026-4116. The most severe, CVE-2026-4112, involves a SQL injection flaw enabling read-only administrators to gain full control. Affected versions include 12.4.3-03245 and earlier, and 12.5.0-02283 and earlier.
